Phulbari tasted freedom on this day in 1971
2013-12-04T00:10:15+06:00 | Our Correspondent, Dinajpur
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/phulbari-tasted-freedom-on-this-day-in-1971

People of Phulbari upazila that tasted freedom on this day in 1971 will recall the occasion with several colourful programmes.

Valiant freedom fighters freed the upazila from Pakistani army by hoisting the flag in the town on December 4.

The Pakistani occupation forces fled Phulbari on the day when the Indian force entered through border points including Jalpaitoli and Rudrani.

With the confirmation of victory, people gathered in the upazila town and rejoiced the victory chanting slogans 'Joy Bangla', led by hundreds of freedom fighters of the area.

On March 25 in 1971, the Pakistani troop launched a crackdown on innocent people with the help of local collaborators following political deadlock in Dhaka.

After the declaration of independence by Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman on March 7, the freedom fighters formed a committee to protect and free Phulbari from the Pakistani forces.

But the Pakistani army carried out arson attacks, looting, and killings of innocent Bangalees in the upazila with the help of their local collaborators. The massacre also forced many people to leave the area for safer places as well take refuge in India.

On April 2, the occupation forces shelled heavily and entered Phulbari, Birampur, Nawabganj, Hakimpur and Ghoraghat upazilas and looted and torched the houses in the area. They also raped women and teenage girls.

Enraged by the incident, local freedom fighters launched a massive attack. The fierce fighting intensified further after the Indian forces joined the freedom fighters. Finally they compelled Pakistani army to retreat.

Freedom Fighter Commander Monsur Ali Sarker hoisted the flag of independent Bangladesh at Phulbari C&B Bungalow in presence of Major PK Singh of Indian forces on the day.
